target_customer: Seniors living in assisted living and senior living communities, paid mainly through Medicare Advantage and value based contracts, with operators as partners
problem: Senior living residents get fragmented primary care and are exposed to hospital risks; on-site clinicians aim to keep them healthier.
business_model: Primary care practice paid by Medicare Advantage plans and value based arrangements
product_category: On-site primary care for senior living residents

founders.name: George Khasin
founders.background_notes: Senior Housing News (Jan 2022): co-founder and CEO; his work on remote monitoring for senior living led him to live in a senior living community for a time. The YC page lists no founder names.

technical_complexity.rationale: Primary care delivery depends on clinical operations, licensing and payer contracts rather than hard software; technology is mostly scheduling and records.

defensibility.rationale: Operator partnerships and Medicare Advantage contracts take time to build, but larger primary care chains were eyeing senior living by 2022 per Senior Housing News.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: By January 2022 Oak Street and Cano were reported to be eyeing senior living and CareMore worked with Welltower on a similar initiative; no acquisition of Pine Park was found.

market_need_then: The YC page frames the need as keeping senior living residents out of hospitals through on-site care; Senior Housing News (Aug 2018) discussed senior living operators pursuing Medicare Advantage opportunities per search result title, not opened.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and patient centered: Bringing the doctor's office to you

branding.brand_signature: Bringing the doctor's office to you tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Calm, generic healthcare naming with no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Pine Park Health began placing primary care clinicians inside senior living communities after YC in Summer 2018. Senior Housing News reported 44 million dollars raised by January 2022 across a 2020 round and a summer 2021 Series B, with about 50 communities served and expansion to San Diego and Phoenix. A WARN notice in Tempe in March 2024 suggests some cuts. It is active and works with over 100 operators per its site.
notes: Founding year conflict: the YC page says 2018, Senior Housing News says 2019. Competitor list left empty: no 2018 dated rival source found; Oak Street, Cano and CareMore appear only in a January 2022 article. Aggregators list a 12.5 million dollar Series A (Sept 2020), a 27 to 27.5 million dollar Series B (July or Sept 2021), a possible second 15 million dollar round (Dec 2023 or Jan 2024) and a seed in Aug 2018, with totals from 39.6 to 58.5 million dollars; none verified so amounts are left null. SHN calls the 2021 round Series B and the 2020 round only a first round of capital, so stage is other. Other founders named by directories (Yoitsu Kamijo, Yingzhe Reginald Fu) are unverified and not recorded. The March 2024 layoff comes from a search summary of WARNTracker, not an opened page. Clinical officer Payam Parvinchiha is not a founder. Update: the 2020 round is now series_a at 12.5M (Seedtable and BounceWatch, aggregators, single database basis; Seedtable lists First Round Capital as lead and Canvas Ventures as participant) and the 2021 series_b at 27.5M dated 2021-07 (Seedtable and CB Insights; BounceWatch says 27.0M in Sept 2021; Senior Housing News confirms a 2021 Series B and 44M total raised). The 2018 seed (Aug 2018, Y Combinator) rests on Seedtable only with no amount: BounceWatch shows 130K from Y Combinator while Employbl shows about 4M with First Round Capital, Gradient and others, so the amount is left null. Canvas Ventures as a 2018 investor is not supported.
